issues: PDF page 1 contains only the cover heading 'M E N U'; not a category, omitted.
No allergy/service/VAT footnotes are printed anywhere in the PDF or docx; footnotes is empty.

Letter-spaced headings were collapsed using word breaks from the docx where the PDF gives none (LE INSALATE, ANTIPASTI CALDI, PRIMI PIATTI, SECONDI PIATTI); wine headings collapsed with the same logic (RARE VINTAGE WINES, RED WINES, WHITE WINES, ROSÉ WINES, PORTO & SEMI SWEET WINES, SPARKLING WINES & CHAMPAGNES).
Section order differs: PDF has ANTIPASTI, LE INSALATE, ANTIPASTI CALDI; docx has ANTIPASTI, ANTIPASTI CALDI, LE INSALATE. PDF order used.
PDF 'R E D W I N E S' (pages 8-9) and 'W H I T E W I N E S' (pages 10-11) are each printed twice as page headers; merged into one category each, with country sub-categories in printed order.

Wine/drinks sections (RARE VINTAGE WINES to SPARKLING WINES & CHAMPAGNES) exist only in the PDF; the docx has no drinks at all. They are named in Italian/English/Turkish only once, so tr = en for all items and categories.

Wine lines (grape / region / country) are printed once and are language-neutral; the same text is stored in both detailTr and detailEn. Country sub-headings (FRANCE, ITALY, TÜRKİYE, ...) are kept as printed and modelled as 'sub' categories.

Wines with two printed prices (e.g. '$ 20' then '$ 100') were split into two items '(glass)' and '(bottle)'. The PDF text does not label them; glass/bottle is inferred from the price pattern (low price first) and should be verified against the printed PDF. Affected: SARAFİN (red, white, rosé), KAVAKLIDERE SELECTION (red, white), CHEVAL NOIR BORDEAUX ROUGE RED WINE, CHEVAL NOIR BORDEAUX (white), CHEVAL NOIR BORDEAUX ROSÉ, KAVAKLIDERE SULTANİYE ($20/$70), KAVAKLIDERE İNCİ DAMLASI ($20/$80), SAN GIOVANNI PERINI PROSECCO EXTRA DRY and BRUT ROSÉ ($15/$50).
Prices '$ 1.000', '$ 1.650', '$ 2.550' use a dot as thousands separator; stored as 1000, 1650, 2550.

Printed typos kept as-is (PDF is authoritative): 'Bordeaux St. Julen', 'CHATEUA D'ESCLANS', 'Coteaux D'aıx En Provence' (dotless i), 'SEMASKA', 'Trevenezie', 'Negrar'; inconsistent casing of 'Italy'/'Germany' vs 'ITALY'/'FRANCE' in grape lines; 'Grenache/Cotes de Provence/FRANCE' without spaces for ROCK ANGEL.
Two-line wine name 'CHÂTEAU CAVALIER' + 'CUVÉE MARAFIENCE COTEAUX PROVENCE ROSÉ' joined into one name. Multi-line grape lines (CANTEMERLE, BEYCHEVELLE) joined with a space.
Doubled spaces removed in 'CHATEAU CORBIN SAINT - ÉMILION  GRAND CRU', 'EPICURO  Z-ELEBRATE ZINFANDEL', 'MONTE  CEPAS MALBEC'. 'SAINT - ÉMILION' and 'SAINT- ÉMILION' hyphen spacing kept as printed.

Duplicate names with different content: SARAFİN (3 reds, 3 whites, 1 rosé), KAVAKLIDERE COTES D'AVANOS (2 whites), CLOUDY BAY (2 whites), GRAND C RESERVE (red $100 Pinot Noir; white $70 Pinot Blanc), LE BIJOU (white $70, rosé $50), PAUL THOMAS SANCERRE (white and rosé), MONTE CEPAS (red MALBEC $50 and white $70). Not errors, but names alone are not unique.

Pizza and some Secondi Piatti (SOGLIOLA, OMBRINA, COSTOLETTE, RIB-EYE, FILETTO, OSSO BUCO, GUANCIA) print TR and EN description on one line separated by ' / '; split into detailTr and detailEn. CERNIA, other food items print them on two lines.
Docx has Russian text next to every PIZZA heading, name and description (e.g. 'PIZZA/ ПИЦЦА', 'PIZZA BISTECCA/ ПИЦЦА БИСТЕККА'); dropped. The PDF has no Russian.

Docx name spelling differs from PDF (PDF used): CARNE CRUDO vs CRUDA ALL'ALBESE; CALAMARI ... CACIO PEPE vs CACIO E PEPE; CODE DI GAMBERI vs GAMBERO; CARCIOFI AVOKADO vs AVOCADO; PARPADELLA AL RAGU vs PAPPARDELLE AL RAGÙ; TAGLIOLINI TARTUFO vs AL TARTUFO; SPAGETTHI/SPAHGETTI vs SPAGHETTI (DI MARE, ALLA BOLOGNESE, AL POMODORO); PASTA CARBONARO vs CARBONARA; PIZZA FOURSTEGION vs PIZZA QUATTRO STAGIONI; COTOLETTE AGNELLO vs COSTOLETTE DI AGNELLO; FILLET DE MANZO vs FILETTO DI MANZO; OSSO BUCCO vs OSSO BUCO.

Docx description differences (PDF used): CERNIA 'lahos balığı ... grouper fish, patato mash with lemon' vs PDF 'Lagos balığı ... Grouper with lemon-infused mashed potatoes' ('Lagos'/'lahos' is probably a misspelling of 'Lahos' in the PDF; verify); docx uses 've' conjunctions where PDF uses commas (SPICY SEAFOOD SOUP, CARPACCIO, FANTASIA DI BURRATA, BRESAOLA, CARNE CRUDA, CARCIOFI, MELANZANE etc.); 'rocket' (docx) vs 'arugula' (PDF); 'Thin sliced' vs 'Thinly sliced'; 'Baked layered pasta' vs 'Layered pasta'; 'Pappardelle with beef ragù' vs 'Pappardelle pasta with beef ragu'; 'Vanilla panna cotta' vs 'Vanilla milk dessert'; 'Chocolate cannelloni dessert' vs 'Chocolate dessert'; 'Zabaione with Marsala wine' vs 'Cream dessert with Marsala wine'; 'Vegetables and smoked beef pizza' vs 'Vegetable and smoked meat pizza'.
No food item exists in only one of the two files; the docx just lacks prices and all wines.
PDF text uses ligature characters (ﬁ, ﬂ, ﬄ), fixed to plain letters (confit, truffle, fillet, filled, flavors, trüflü).
